j-kym.title: Jérôme Kym (Switzerland) - Profile, career and playing style | AnalisiTennis
j-kym.description: Profile of Jérôme Kym: the young Swiss player, his playing style, preferred surfaces and the key moments of his career.
j-kym.intro: A young Swiss raised in the wake of his country's great tradition, Jérôme Kym has established himself as one of the most solid prospects in Swiss tennis.
stats: Aggressive baseline game, at home on hard courts

p: Jérôme Kym belongs to the generation of Swiss players who grew up with the weighty legacy left by champions such as Roger Federer and Stan Wawrinka. Born in 2003 and trained in the canton of Aargau, he followed the classic path of a talented European player: junior tournaments, early experience on the minor circuits and a gradual adaptation to the pace of professional tennis. From his first seasons he was flagged as one of the profiles the Swiss federation backed with conviction, to the point of involving him very young in the Davis Cup team.

His path, as often happens with young players, has not been linear: a few physical setbacks slowed his rise at times, forcing him to rebuild his fitness and his ranking patiently. This very ability to return after difficulties has become one of the defining traits of his development.

Kym is a baseliner with a robust physique and a solid frame, qualities that let him sustain intense rallies without losing power. His tennis is built on a heavy forehand, the shot around which he constructs most of his initiatives, and on a serve that, when well calibrated, earns him free points and the chance to dictate from the very first ball.

The two-handed backhand is a reliable support, used mainly to keep depth and change direction, while he constantly looks to move around the return to attack with his best shot. He is an offensive but pragmatic player, who prefers to command the rally rather than rely on pure defence. Over the years the clearest work has been on consistency: turning good days into repeatable results and better managing tense moments against more experienced opponents.

The features of his game make him particularly comfortable on fast surfaces, where his serve and forehand pay off and rallies tend to shorten in his favour. Hard courts, indoors included, are the environment where he has historically produced his most linear and productive tennis.

On clay he has to negotiate slower rhythms and longer rallies that test patience and point construction: a surface that demands adjustments but can also help him refine his variety. On grass, like many of his countrymen, he has potentially suitable weapons thanks to his serve, even if it is the surface where the international game is decided on the finest details.

In his development, Kym has built his ranking mainly through the Challenger circuit, where he has collected results that have brought him steadily closer to the positions that open the doors of the main draws.

Key points of his journey: a number of notable Challenger results, useful for climbing the ranking; his involvement in the Swiss Davis Cup team, a sign of the federation's trust; and his ability to come back after the physical difficulties of his early seasons.

He remains a player firmly in his breakthrough phase, with a margin for improvement that still looks wide. That is why his name is followed closely by those watching the future of Swiss tennis: the technical base is there, and the direction of his work hints at room for further growth.

faq.q: What is Jérôme Kym's playing style?
faq.a: Jérôme Kym is an aggressive baseliner built around a heavy forehand and a solid serve, most effective on hard courts.
Jérôme Kym is a male player from Switzerland, born on 7 April 2003.

faq.q: What is Jérôme Kym's best surface?
faq.a: Kym is most comfortable on hard courts, indoors included, where his serve and forehand shorten the rallies in his favour.

harriet-dart.title: Harriet Dart (United Kingdom) - Profile, career and playing style | AnalisiTennis
harriet-dart.description: Editorial profile of Harriet Dart, the British WTA player: her playing style, preferred surfaces and the maiden title won in Guangzhou in 2026.
harriet-dart.intro: Harriet Dart embodies the resilience of British women's tennis: a combative player rewarded in 2026 with a maiden WTA title after a long apprenticeship.
stats: Offensive game based on serve and forehand, best on grass

p: Harriet Dart, born in Hampstead, north London, on 28 July 1996, is one of the most recognisable figures in British women's tennis of recent years. Raised within the British set-up, she built her career patiently, going through the long apprenticeship of the minor tournaments before carving out a stable place on the main tour, reaching a career-high No. 70 in September 2024. Dedication and consistency have become her trademark; she regularly represents her country in team competitions and has become a familiar face for the home crowd.

Right-handed, with a two-handed backhand, Dart plays a game founded on intensity and physical commitment rather than pure elegance. Hers is a solid baseline game, supported by a forehand that can turn into an attacking weapon when she finds the right moment to take the initiative. Without the leverage of the taller players, she compensates on serve with timing and with her search for angles, and on her best days the shot still lets her open up the court and command the rally from the first strokes.

The trait that defines her most, however, is her character. Dart is a fighter who rarely gives away free points and who can drag herself into a match even when the opponent's technical level is higher. This tenacity makes her especially awkward in tight contests, where handling the decisive moments and break points often makes the difference.

Like many British players, Dart finds grass the surface most suited to her nature. Fast courts reward her serve and her tendency to shorten the rally, and it is no coincidence that her most keenly felt performances often come during the grass season, in front of a crowd that backs her warmly.

That does not mean she is uncomfortable elsewhere. On hard courts, which make up much of the calendar, she has produced competitive tennis, using her baseline consistency and her ability to sustain a high tempo. Clay is probably the terrain least suited to her characteristics, since the longer rally times tend to reduce the effectiveness of her attacking shots; even there, though, her combativeness has brought her satisfactions.

Dart's path was built for a long time on the minor circuits, where she won seven singles titles that gave her the ranking and confidence to establish herself on the main tour. The reward came only in 2026, at the age of thirty, with a maiden WTA title at the Guangzhou Open: in the final she beat Austria's Lilli Tagger 4-6, 6-3, 6-4, having also defeated Paula Badosa earlier in the week. The same season brought her first two doubles trophies, in Nottingham and Prague.

Among the most significant chapters are her appearances on the great Grand Slam stages, in particular those played at home: at Wimbledon she reached the third round in 2019 and again in 2024, her best result at a major. Add to that her frequent call-ups to the national team, with whom she has played the Billie Jean King Cup since 2019, helping Great Britain to the semi-finals in 2022 and 2024.

Overall, Harriet Dart's career tells the story of a player who has made consistency and fighting spirit her strengths, turning daily hard work into a dependable and respected presence in women's tennis.

faq.q: What is Harriet Dart's playing style?
faq.a: Harriet Dart plays an offensive, physical baseline game built on her serve and forehand, and is at her best on grass.
Harriet Dart is a female player from the United Kingdom, born on 28 July 1996.

faq.q: What is Harriet Dart's best surface?
faq.a: Dart is most effective on grass, where her serve and her attacking instincts are best rewarded.
